driver_name.description: Name of the LIRC driver to start (used for compatibility with some LIRC versions).

driver_type.description: Name of the LIRC driver module to use (e.g., 'default', 'lirc_serial', 'gpio_rcv').

hardware_types.description:
List of supported hardware types (e.g., 'default', 'hauppauge', 'atiusb').
Note: This is a global config parameter, but `lircd.conf(5)` does not document global config
sections outside of remote blocks. However, `driver_name`, `device_path`, etc. are also
not documented in `lircd.conf(5)` as global keys, only within remote blocks or as
command-line options. The man page states: 'The file has two purposes: to provide timing
information to the driver... and to provide a mapping from button presses...'.
It does NOT document global keys like `start_driver`, `device`, `driver`, `hwtypes`.
Those belong in `lircd.conf` (the config file for lircd service args) or are handled
by command line args/env. However, the prompt says 'Package/service: lircd.conf'.

remotes.description:
List of remote controls with their button mappings.
Items must have a unique 'name'.
Supported optional fields per lircd.conf(5):
- flags: pipe-separated list of flags (RC5, RC6, SPACE_ENC, etc.)
- bits: integer
- eps: integer (percent)
- aeps: integer (microseconds)
- gap: integer (microseconds)
- suppress_repeat: integer
- manual_sort: 0 or 1
- include: "<path>"
- header: <pulse> <space>
- three: <pulse> <space>
- two: <pulse> <space>
- one: <pulse> <space>
- zero: <pulse> <space>
- ptrail: <pulse>
- plead: <pulse>
- foot: <pulse> <space>
- repeat: <pulse> <space>
- pre_data_bits: integer
- pre_data: hexadecimal
- post_data_bits: integer
- post_data: hexadecimal
- pre: <pulse> <space>
- post: <pulse> <space>
- repeat_gap: <space>
- min_repeat: integer
- toggle_bit: integer
- toggle_bit_mask: hexadecimal
- repeat_mask: hexadecimal
- frequency: integer (hertz)
- duty_cycle: integer (1-100)
- raw_codes block OR codes block.
